<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918005_theRebbe_76" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918005_theRebbe_76__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the novelty of the future redemption is not the existence of miracles, but that G-d will show them openly, whereas now even great miracles from the level of "Levado" are hidden.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And to add,</t>
    <t s="1">that based on this we can also explain what the verse precisely states, "I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="2">that the main novelty is not that there will be wonders then, but rather that G-d will show the wonders,</t>
    <t s="3">for wonders exist even now,</t>
    <t s="4">and even great wonders that are drawn from the aspect of "Levado" (Alone) exist,</t>
    <t s="5">and the novelty in the future redemption is that then it will be "I will show him wonders."</t>
    <t s="6">For now,</t>
    <t s="7">the miracles drawn from the aspect of "Levado" are in a manner that only He alone knows that it is a miracle,</t>
    <t s="8">and in the future redemption it will be "I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="9">that the miracle within them will be seen in revelation.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses that the future wonders will surpass even the miracles of the Exodus, being a wonder relative to that wonder, and questions what the novelty of "showing" is regarding miracles above nature.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">D)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the two types of miracles</t>
    <t s="2">(miracles above nature and miracles clothed in nature)</t>
    <t s="3">each have an advantage20.</t>
    <t s="4">And since in the future all matters will be at the ultimate perfection,</t>
    <t s="5">it must be said,</t>
    <t s="6">that what is written "I will show him wonders" is not only regarding miracles clothed in nature</t>
    <t s="7">(that in the future the miracle within them will be seen in revelation,</t>
    <t s="8">as above in section Gimmel),</t>
    <t s="9">but also regarding miracles that are not clothed in nature.</t>
    <t s="10">And this is also understood from that which it says that the wonders of the future redemption will be "as the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="11">for the miracles of the Exodus were above nature21.</t>
    <t s="12">And to add,</t>
    <t s="13">that the reason miracles are called "wonders" (niflaos) is</t>
    <t s="14">(simply)</t>
    <t s="15">because they are a wonder that has no place in nature,</t>
    <t s="16">and from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="17">that what is written "I will show him wonders" and it is brought in the Midrash that the wonders of the future redemption will be greater than the wonders of the Exodus</t>
    <t s="18">[to the extent that they will be wonders relative to the wonders of the Exodus]</t>
    <t s="19">— the intention in this is,</t>
    <t s="20">that the wonder</t>
    <t s="21">(above nature)</t>
    <t s="22">in the miracles of the future redemption is a wonder also relative to the wonder of the miracles of the Exodus22.</t>
    <t s="23">And we need to understand what is meant by "I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="24">for seemingly,</t>
    <t s="25">according to the interpretation that "I will show him wonders" refers to miracles above nature</t>
    <t s="26">(and especially since the above-nature of the future wonders will be even greater than the above-nature of the miracles of the Exodus),</t>
    <t s="27">what is the novelty in that they will see the wonders?</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that miracles above nature are called wonders because their essence is not grasped, while miracles clothed in nature reveal their essence, as explained by the Mitteler Rebbe.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">E)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing what was brought above</t>
    <t s="2">(section Gimmel)</t>
    <t s="3">that the root of the drawing down of miracles whose owner does not recognize his miracle is from the aspect of "Levado."</t>
    <t s="4">And we need to understand,</t>
    <t s="5">how is it possible that the garments of nature will conceal and hide a miracle drawn from the aspect of "Levado"?</t>
    <t s="6">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="7">that the advantage of miracles clothed in nature over miracles above nature,</t>
    <t s="8">is as explained by the Mitteler Rebbe in Shaar HaEmunah23,</t>
    <t s="9">that by the miracle being clothed in nature, it comes into revelation.</t>
    <t s="10">For regarding miracles that are not clothed in nature,</t>
    <t s="11">one knows only their existence, not their essence.</t>
    <t s="12">Like the miracle of the resurrection of the dead,</t>
    <t s="13">for although one sees in actuality that initially there was a dead person and now he is alive,</t>
    <t s="14">one does not know or comprehend how he came back to life.</t>
    <t s="15">And so it is with all miracles above nature.</t>
    <t s="16">Therefore these miracles are called "wonders" (niflaos),</t>
    <t s="17">for a wonder is that which is not grasped by the intellect</t>
    <t s="18">[to the extent,</t>
    <t s="19">that when a person sees a wondrous thing he is astonished by it,</t>
    <t s="20">for astonishment is the nullification of the intellect24].</t>
    <t s="21">And by the miracle being clothed in nature,</t>
    <t s="22">it comes into revelation,</t>
    <t s="23">for one grasps its essence.</t>
    <t s="24">Like the miracle of Purim,</t>
    <t s="25">where one knows and comprehends how the decree was nullified</t>
    <t s="26">(which was through Esther, etc.).</t>
    <t s="27">And likewise the four who are required to give thanks,</t>
    <t s="28">one knows and comprehends how the sick person was healed</t>
    <t s="29">(which was through medicinal herbs),</t>
    <t s="30">and so forth.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
